lines.raw: Lesson 1: What is Eligibility Data?
lines.say: Lesson 1: What is Eligibility Data?

lines.raw: Before any bill is paid, someone asks: was this person covered on that day?
lines.say: Before any bill is paid, someone asks: was this person covered on that day?

lines.raw: In this lesson you will:
lines.say: In this lesson you will:

lines.raw: Explain in one sentence what "eligibility data" means.
lines.say: Explain in one sentence what "eligibility data" means.

lines.raw: Know why the insurer checks eligibility before paying every claim.
lines.say: Know why the insurer checks eligibility before paying every claim.

lines.raw: See where eligibility sits next to medical and pharmacy data.
lines.say: See where eligibility sits next to medical and pharmacy data.

lines.raw: Start with something you already know.
lines.say: Start with something you already know.

scenes.section: Start with something you already know

lines.raw: Think about a gym membership in Kathmandu.
lines.say: Think about a gym membership in Kathmandu.

lines.raw: When you walk in, the person at the desk looks you up.
lines.say: When you walk in, the person at the desk looks you up.

lines.raw: Are you a **member**?
lines.say: Are you a member?

lines.raw: Which **package** did you buy?
lines.say: Which package did you buy?

lines.raw: Is it still **valid today**, or did it run out last month?
lines.say: Is it still valid today, or did it run out last month?

lines.raw: Only then do they let you in.
lines.say: Only then do they let you in.

scenes.section: Start with something you already know

lines.raw: Health insurance works the same way.
lines.say: Health insurance works the same way.

lines.raw: Before an insurer pays a single rupee or dollar, it checks its list of members: is this person **covered**, by **which plan**, and was the cover **active on the day** of the visit?
lines.say: Before an insurer pays a single rupee or dollar, it checks its list of members: is this person covered, by which plan, and was the cover active on the day of the visit?

lines.raw: That list is called **eligibility data** (also called **enrollment** or **membership** data).
lines.say: That list is called eligibility data (also called enrollment or membership data).

scenes.section: Start with something you already know

lines.raw: Simple definition.
lines.say: Simple definition.

lines.raw: Eligibility data is the record of **who is covered**, **by which plan**, and **from which date to which date**.
lines.say: Eligibility data is the record of who is covered, by which plan, and from which date to which date.

lines.raw: It is the insurer's list of members, with a start and end date for every person.
lines.say: It is the insurer's list of members, with a start and end date for every person.

lines.raw: Meet our people.
lines.say: Meet our people.

lines.raw: This course follows three people.
lines.say: This course follows three people.

lines.raw: **Ram** works at a tech startup in Kathmandu and is covered by its group health policy.
lines.say: Ram works at a tech startup in Kathmandu and is covered by its group health policy.

lines.raw: **Sita** is an accountant in Kathmandu who contributes to the Social Security Fund (SSF).
lines.say: Sita is an accountant in Kathmandu who contributes to the Social Security Fund (S S F).

lines.raw: **Emily** is an office worker in Texas, USA, with health insurance through her employer.
lines.say: Emily is an office worker in Texas, U S A, with health insurance through her employer.

lines.raw: For each of them we ask one question: not "what care did they get?" but "**were they covered when they got it?**"
lines.say: For each of them we ask one question: not "what care did they get?" but "were they covered when they got it?"

lines.raw: In Nepal: Is Ram's and Sita's cover active?
lines.say: In Nepal: Is Ram's and Sita's cover active?

lines.raw: With private insurance:
lines.say: With private insurance:

lines.raw: **Ram** is covered by a **group health policy** that his startup buys from a private insurer.
lines.say: Ram is covered by a group health policy that his startup buys from a private insurer.

lines.raw: The policy has a **start date** and an **end date**, usually one year.
lines.say: The policy has a start date and an end date, usually one year.

lines.raw: Each year the startup must **renew** it.
lines.say: Each year the startup must renew it.

lines.raw: When Ram sends a claim, the insurer first checks: was the policy **active** on the date of Ram's treatment?
lines.say: When Ram sends a claim, the insurer first checks: was the policy active on the date of Ram's treatment?

lines.raw: Was Ram still an employee on the list?
lines.say: Was Ram still an employee on the list?

lines.raw: If the startup forgot to renew, or Ram had already left the company, the claim is rejected, no matter how real the illness was.
lines.say: If the startup forgot to renew, or Ram had already left the company, the claim is rejected, no matter how real the illness was.

lines.raw: With the Social Security Fund:
lines.say: With the Social Security Fund:

lines.raw: **Sita** is covered because she **contributes to SSF** through her employer.
lines.say: Sita is covered because she contributes to S S F through her employer.

lines.raw: When she visits an SSF-listed hospital, the hospital checks her **SSF ID** and whether her **contributions are up to date**.
lines.say: When she visits an S S F listed hospital, the hospital checks her S S F I D and whether her contributions are up to date.

lines.raw: If her employer stopped depositing contributions, SSF may not treat her as eligible, even though she has an SSF ID card.
lines.say: If her employer stopped depositing contributions, S S F may not treat her as eligible, even though she has an S S F I D card.

lines.raw: So "Do you have a card?" is not enough.
lines.say: So "Do you have a card?" is not enough.

lines.raw: The real question is "Is your cover **active today**?".
lines.say: The real question is "Is your cover active today?".

lines.raw: In the US: Emily's cover in Texas.
lines.say: In the U S: Emily's cover in Texas.

lines.raw: **Emily Carter** works at a company that gives her **health insurance** (an "employer plan").
lines.say: Emily Carter works at a company that gives her health insurance (an "employer plan").

lines.raw: Her insurer keeps a record for her: member ID **M1001**, her plan, and the date her cover started.
lines.say: Her insurer keeps a record for her: member I D M 1 0 0 1, her plan, and the date her cover started.

lines.raw: Her plan has a **$1,000 deductible** and **20% coinsurance** (the Medical course works through her claims on this plan in detail).
lines.say: Her plan has a 1000 dollars deductible and 20 percent coinsurance (the Medical course works through her claims on this plan in detail).

lines.raw: Every time a claim for Emily arrives, the insurer looks up M1001 and checks the **service date** against her coverage dates before paying.
lines.say: Every time a claim for Emily arrives, the insurer looks up M 1 0 0 1 and checks the service date against her coverage dates before paying.

lines.raw: What does eligibility data contain?
lines.say: What does eligibility data contain?

lines.raw: Here is a quick table.
lines.say: Here is a quick table.

lines.raw: **Who**. What it includes: Name, date of birth, gender, address, member ID. Emily's example: Emily Carter, born 14 Aug 1990, female, Austin TX, M1001.
lines.say: Who. What it includes: Name, date of birth, gender, address, member I D. Emily's example: Emily Carter, born 14 Aug 1990, female, Austin T X, M 1 0 0 1.

lines.raw: **Family link**. What it includes: Who the main policyholder is, and how each person is related to them. Emily's example: Emily is the policyholder herself (relationship: self).
lines.say: Family link. What it includes: Who the main policyholder is, and how each person is related to them. Emily's example: Emily is the policyholder herself (relationship: self).

lines.raw: **Which plan**. What it includes: The employer group, the plan, the type of insurance. Emily's example: Her employer's group, a PPO plan, commercial insurance.
lines.say: Which plan. What it includes: The employer group, the plan, the type of insurance. Emily's example: Her employer's group, a P P O plan, commercial insurance.

lines.raw: **When**. What it includes: The **effective date** (start) and **termination date** (end) of cover. Emily's example: Started 1 Jan 2022, no end date yet.
lines.say: When. What it includes: The effective date (start) and termination date (end) of cover. Emily's example: Started 1 Jan 2022, no end date yet.

lines.raw: **Other insurance**. What it includes: Whether the person has a second insurance, and which pays first. Emily's example: None for Emily herself.
lines.say: Other insurance. What it includes: Whether the person has a second insurance, and which pays first. Emily's example: None for Emily herself.

lines.raw: Coming up.
lines.say: Coming up.

lines.raw: You will learn about each group in later lessons: plans in lesson 2, family links in lesson 3, dates in lesson 4, how the data arrives in lesson 5 and other insurance in lesson 6.
lines.say: You will learn about each group in later lessons: plans in lesson 2, family links in lesson 3, dates in lesson 4, how the data arrives in lesson 5 and other insurance in lesson 6.

lines.raw: Why check eligibility before every claim?
lines.say: Why check eligibility before every claim?

scenes.section: Why check eligibility before every claim?

lines.raw: **People change jobs.**
lines.say: People change jobs.

lines.raw: When Emily leaves her company, her employer cover ends.
lines.say: When Emily leaves her company, her employer cover ends.

lines.raw: A claim after that date should not be paid by this plan.
lines.say: A claim after that date should not be paid by this plan.

lines.raw: **Families change.**
lines.say: Families change.

lines.raw: A baby is born, a couple marries, a child grows up and leaves the plan.
lines.say: A baby is born, a couple marries, a child grows up and leaves the plan.

lines.raw: **Plans change.**
lines.say: Plans change.

lines.raw: Each year an employer may switch plans or insurers.
lines.say: Each year an employer may switch plans or insurers.

lines.raw: **Money is at stake.**
lines.say: Money is at stake.

lines.raw: Paying for someone who was not covered is a loss, and getting it back later is slow and difficult.
lines.say: Paying for someone who was not covered is a loss, and getting it back later is slow and difficult.

scenes.section: Why check eligibility before every claim?

lines.raw: Where this fits.
lines.say: Where this fits.

lines.raw: When an insurer processes a claim, one of the first steps is the **eligibility check**, and one of the most common denial reasons is **"Not eligible: the patient was not covered on the service date"**.
lines.say: When an insurer processes a claim, one of the first steps is the eligibility check, and one of the most common denial reasons is "Not eligible: the patient was not covered on the service date".

lines.raw: The Medical course follows the whole claim journey; this course explains the data behind that check.
lines.say: The Medical course follows the whole claim journey; this course explains the data behind that check.

lines.raw: Eligibility is the "who" table every claim joins to.
lines.say: Eligibility is the "who" table every claim joins to.

scenes.section: Eligibility is the "who" table every claim joins to

lines.raw: An insurer receives several kinds of data.
lines.say: An insurer receives several kinds of data.

lines.raw: Medical and pharmacy claims say **what happened**.
lines.say: Medical and pharmacy claims say what happened.

lines.raw: Eligibility says **who was allowed to have it paid for**.
lines.say: Eligibility says who was allowed to have it paid for.

lines.raw: Every claim carries a member ID, and analysts link it to the eligibility table using that ID and the service date.
lines.say: Every claim carries a member I D, and analysts link it to the eligibility table using that I D and the service date.

scenes.section: Eligibility is the "who" table every claim joins to

lines.raw: Here is a quick table.
lines.say: Here is a quick table.

lines.raw: **Eligibility**. What it tells you: Who is covered, by which plan, from which date to which date. Nepal comparison: Is Sita's SSF contribution up to date? Is Ram's policy still running?
lines.say: Eligibility. What it tells you: Who is covered, by which plan, from which date to which date. Nepal comparison: Is Sita's S S F contribution up to date? Is Ram's policy still running?

lines.raw: **Medical**. What it tells you: Doctor and hospital services. Nepal comparison: OPD, admission, surgery bills.
lines.say: Medical. What it tells you: Doctor and hospital services. Nepal comparison: O P D, admission, surgery bills.

lines.raw: **Pharmacy**. What it tells you: Medicines bought with a prescription. Nepal comparison: Bill from the medical shop / pharmacy.
lines.say: Pharmacy. What it tells you: Medicines bought with a prescription. Nepal comparison: Bill from the medical shop or pharmacy.

lines.raw: **Lab**. What it tells you: Test results. Nepal comparison: The lab report you collect the next day.
lines.say: Lab. What it tells you: Test results. Nepal comparison: The lab report you collect the next day.

scenes.section: Eligibility is the "who" table every claim joins to

lines.raw: Think of a school register.
lines.say: Think of a school register.

lines.raw: A school has an **attendance register** (who is enrolled in which class, since when) and **mark sheets** (what each student scored).
lines.say: A school has an attendance register (who is enrolled in which class, since when) and mark sheets (what each student scored).

lines.raw: A mark sheet for a student who is not on the register makes no sense.
lines.say: A mark sheet for a student who is not on the register makes no sense.

lines.raw: Eligibility is the register; claims are the mark sheets.
lines.say: Eligibility is the register; claims are the mark sheets.

lines.raw: You always check the register first.
lines.say: You always check the register first.

lines.say: Want to know which plan paid for a claim?

lines.say: Want to check a claim is valid?

lines.say: You need the coverage dates.

lines.raw: Key takeaways.
lines.say: Key takeaways.

lines.raw: Eligibility data = who is covered, by which plan, and from when to when.
lines.say: Eligibility data = who is covered, by which plan, and from when to when.

lines.raw: Insurers check eligibility on the **service date** before paying any claim.
lines.say: Insurers check eligibility on the service date before paying any claim.

lines.raw: Having a card is not enough; cover must be **active on that day**.
lines.say: Having a card is not enough; cover must be active on that day.

lines.raw: Eligibility is the "who" table that medical and pharmacy claims join to, using member ID and dates.
lines.say: Eligibility is the "who" table that medical and pharmacy claims join to, using member I D and dates.
